# Model and source

Aruldhas 2019 fitted two separate population PK models -- one for isoniazid
and one for rifampicin -- to steady-state profiles from the same children, and
used them to evaluate Indian paediatric dosing regimens. The library carries
them as two files that share this vignette.

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Aruldhas_2019_isoniazid"))$reference`
* Isoniazid: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Aruldhas_2019_isoniazid"))$description`
* Rifampicin: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Aruldhas_2019_rifampicin"))$description`
* Article: [Br J Clin Pharmacol. 2019;85(3):644-654](https://doi.org/10.1111/bcp.13846)

# Population

The study enrolled 41 children and adolescents aged 2-16 years (median 7,
IQR 3.5-13) at Christian Medical College, Vellore, India, newly diagnosed with
pulmonary (n = 36) or lymph-node (n = 5) tuberculosis (Table 2). Median body
weight was 19.5 kg (IQR 13.7-33.7); 12 of 41 were girls. Children with relapse,
multidrug-resistant tuberculosis or HIV co-infection were excluded. Isoniazid,
rifampicin, pyrazinamide and ethambutol were given either daily (WHO regimen,
n = 14) or thrice weekly (national RNTCP directly observed regimen, n = 27) at
the same per-occasion dose (Table 1, Regimen 2). Plasma was sampled during the
last 2 weeks of the 8-week intensive phase, pre-dose and 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5,
4 and 6 h after an overnight-fasted dose. The isoniazid model used 290
concentrations from 39 children and the rifampicin model 284 concentrations
from 39 children.

# Source trace

| Element | Isoniazid | Rifampicin | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Disposition | one compartment | one compartment | Results, both 'Pharmacokinetic properties' sections |
| Absorption | 5 transit compartments, ka = ktr | 9 transit compartments, ka = ktr | Results; Tables 3, 4 'No. of trans comp' |
| ktr | 6 / MTT | 10 / MTT | Savic transit chain; checked against published Tmax below |
| MTT | 0.547 h | 0.932 h | Table 3 / Table 4 |
| CL/F | 2.59 L/h slow, 7.79 L/h fast (mixture) | 8.11 L/h | Table 3 / Table 4 |
| V/F | 29.7 L | 44.7 L | Table 3 / Table 4 |
| F | 1 (fixed) | 1 (fixed) | Methods; Tables 3, 4 |
| Allometry | WT/19.4 kg, exponents 0.75 (CL) and 1 (V), fixed | same | Methods; Tables 3, 4 footnotes |
| BSV (%CV) | V 23.4, MTT 68.2, F 41.8 | V 42, MTT 52.2, F 68.0 | Tables 3, 4 |
| Residual error | additive on log scale, variance 0.0967 | additive on log scale, variance 0.271 | Methods; Tables 3, 4 'RUV' |
| Fast-acetylator fraction | 31% (printed; see Errata) | -- | Results; Table 3 footnote; Discussion |
| Regimens 1-4 | Table 1 | Table 1 | Table 1 |

```{r models}
mod_inh <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Aruldhas_2019_isoniazid"))
mod_rif <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Aruldhas_2019_rifampicin"))
```

# Shared simulation helpers

The paper simulated 1000 children at every integer body weight from 6 to
30 kg (Methods, 'Dose optimization'). Rather than a large Monte Carlo cohort,
the replications below integrate over the between-subject variability
deterministically:

* relative bioavailability F scales every concentration, so its log-normal
  variability is integrated analytically (`pnorm()` over its omega);
* the V/F and MTT etas are integrated with a 9 x 9 Gauss-Hermite grid, solved
  at every weight from 6 to 30 kg;
* CL/F carries no between-subject variability, so steady-state
  `AUC0-24 = F * Dose / CL` is exact.

This makes every number in the replication tables reproducible to the digit,
independently of the random-number stream.

```{r helpers}
# Gauss-Hermite nodes and weights for a standard normal (Golub-Welsch).
gauss_hermite <- function(k) {
  b <- sqrt(seq_len(k - 1))
  jac <- matrix(0, k, k)
  jac[cbind(1:(k - 1), 2:k)] <- b
  jac[cbind(2:k, 1:(k - 1))] <- b
  e <- eigen(jac, symmetric = TRUE)
  list(z = e$values, w = e$vectors[1, ]^2)
}

# Table 1 weight bands. `lower` holds the lower band edges in kg.
band_dose <- function(wt, lower, dose) dose[findInterval(wt, lower)]
dose_inh <- list(
  "Regimen 1" = function(wt) band_dose(wt, c(6, 11, 18, 26), c(75, 150, 225, 300)),
  "Regimen 2" = function(wt) band_dose(wt, c(6, 8, 12, 16, 18, 23), c(75, 112.5, 150, 187.5, 225, 300)),
  "Regimen 3" = function(wt) band_dose(wt, c(4, 8, 12, 16, 25, 30), c(50, 100, 150, 200, 225, 250))
)
dose_rif <- list(
  "Regimen 1" = dose_inh[["Regimen 1"]],
  "Regimen 2" = dose_inh[["Regimen 2"]],
  "Regimen 3" = function(wt) band_dose(wt, c(4, 8, 12, 16, 25, 30), c(75, 150, 225, 300, 375, 450)),
  "Regimen 4" = function(wt) {
    ifelse(wt <= 11, 35 * wt, band_dose(wt, c(12, 15, 20, 24, 28), c(450, 600, 750, 900, 1050)))
  }
)

omega_sd <- function(mod, eta) sqrt(mod$omega[eta, eta])

# Grid of (weight, V eta, MTT eta, mixture class) nodes with their
# quadrature weights.
make_grid <- function(mod, classes, k = 9) {
  gh <- gauss_hermite(k)
  g <- expand.grid(WT = 6:30, i = seq_len(k), j = seq_len(k), MIX_FAST_ELIM = classes)
  g$etalvc <- omega_sd(mod, "etalvc") * gh$z[g$i]
  g$etalmtt <- omega_sd(mod, "etalmtt") * gh$z[g$j]
  g$etalfdepot <- 0
  g$wq <- gh$w[g$i] * gh$w[g$j]
  g$id <- seq_len(nrow(g))
  g
}

# Steady-state concentrations after a 1-mg daily dose (15 daily doses, the
# last interval observed every 0.05 h) at every grid node, with F = 1.
# Etas are carried as event-table columns on a zeroRe() model, so each node
# is solved at exactly its own eta values.
solve_unit <- function(mod, grid) {
  dose_times <- seq(0, 24 * 14, by = 24)
  obs_times <- 24 * 14 + seq(0, 24, by = 0.05)
  cols <- c("id", "WT", "MIX_FAST_ELIM", "etalvc", "etalmtt", "etalfdepot")
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    expand.grid(id = grid$id, time = dose_times) |>
      dplyr::mutate(amt = 1, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
    expand.grid(id = grid$id, time = obs_times) |>
      dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    dplyr::left_join(grid[, cols], by = "id") |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
  sim <- suppressWarnings(
    rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), ev, returnType = "data.frame")
  )
  sim$tad <- sim$time - 24 * 14
  sim
}

# Probability that F * dose * c1 exceeds (or falls below) a threshold,
# integrated over the grid and the analytic F distribution.
p_above <- function(conc1, dose, wq, omega_f, thr) {
  sum(wq * stats::pnorm(log(dose * conc1 / thr) / omega_f)) / sum(wq)
}

# Quantile of the mixture distribution of F * dose * c1 over the grid.
mix_quantile <- function(prob, conc1, dose, wq, omega_f, upper = Inf) {
  cdf <- function(x) sum(wq * stats::pnorm(log(x / (dose * conc1)) / omega_f)) / sum(wq)
  total <- if (is.finite(upper)) cdf(upper) else 1
  stats::uniroot(function(x) cdf(x) - prob * total, c(1e-4, 1e4), tol = 1e-8)$root
}
```

```{r grid-solve}
grid_inh <- make_grid(mod_inh, classes = c(0, 1))
grid_rif <- make_grid(mod_rif, classes = 0)
sim_inh <- solve_unit(mod_inh, grid_inh)
sim_rif <- solve_unit(mod_rif, grid_rif)

# Each node's solve must carry its own eta: check V/F against the closed form.
v_chk <- sim_inh |>
  dplyr::filter(tad == 0) |>
  dplyr::select(id, WT, vc) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::transmute(grid_inh, id, eta_v = etalvc), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(v_expected = 29.7 * exp(eta_v) * WT / 19.4)
stopifnot(max(abs(v_chk$vc / v_chk$v_expected - 1)) < 1e-8)

unit_cmax <- function(sim, grid) {
  per_node <- sim |>
    dplyr::group_by(id) |>
    dplyr::summarise(cmax1 = max(Cc), tmax = tad[which.max(Cc)], .groups = "drop")
  dplyr::left_join(grid, per_node, by = "id")
}
nodes_inh <- unit_cmax(sim_inh, grid_inh)
nodes_rif <- unit_cmax(sim_rif, grid_rif)
of_inh <- omega_sd(mod_inh, "etalfdepot")
of_rif <- omega_sd(mod_rif, "etalfdepot")
```

# Transit-chain convention: typical-value Tmax

Both models set the absorption rate equal to the transit rate, so the mean
transit time spans every first-order transfer from the dosing compartment to
the central compartment: `n + 1` of them for `n` transit compartments. The
alternative reading, `ktr = n / MTT`, delays the peak. The published median
Tmax (Tables 3 and 4, secondary parameters) separates the two.

```{r tmax}
typical <- function(nodes) nodes |> dplyr::filter(abs(etalvc) < 1e-12, abs(etalmtt) < 1e-12, WT == 19)
tmax_tab <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  typical(nodes_inh) |>
    dplyr::transmute(Model = ifelse(MIX_FAST_ELIM == 1, "Isoniazid, fast", "Isoniazid, slow"), tmax, published = 1.10),
  typical(nodes_rif) |> dplyr::transmute(Model = "Rifampicin", tmax, published = 1.59)
)
knitr::kable(
  tmax_tab |> dplyr::rename("Typical Tmax at 19 kg (h)" = tmax, "Published median Tmax (h)" = published),
  digits = 2
)
stopifnot(
  all(abs(tmax_tab$tmax - tmax_tab$published) < 0.12)
)
```

With `ktr = n / MTT` the same solve gives about 1.19-1.36 h for isoniazid and
1.72 h for rifampicin, further from the published values in every case.

# Residual error: variance, not SD

Tables 3 and 4 print the residual error as a bare 'RUV' with an RSE and a
bootstrap 95% CI. The between-subject variability rows of the same tables are
on the %CV scale, and for those the CI width is consistent with the RSE
(about `2 x 1.96 x RSE`). For the RUV rows the CI is twice as wide as the RSE
implies, which is what a variance whose RSE is reported on the SD scale looks
like (the relative uncertainty of a variance is twice that of its SD). The
models therefore take `expSd = sqrt(RUV)`.

```{r ruv-scale}
ci_rows <- data.frame(
  Row = c("INH RUV", "RIF RUV", "INH BSV V", "INH BSV MTT", "INH BSV F", "RIF BSV V", "RIF BSV MTT", "RIF BSV F"),
  est = c(0.0967, 0.271, 23.4, 68.2, 41.8, 42, 52.2, 68.0),
  rse = c(9.79, 8.96, 14.1, 13.9, 12.1, 12.6, 12.7, 16.6),
  lo = c(0.0639, 0.191, 16.9, 49.3, 30.1, 31.1, 39.7, 40.0),
  hi = c(0.141, 0.379, 30.2, 94.3, 51.9, 53.9, 68.0, 95.6)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = ((hi - lo) / est) / (2 * 1.96 * rse / 100))
knitr::kable(
  ci_rows |> dplyr::rename("Table row" = Row, "Estimate" = est, "RSE (%)" = rse, "CI low" = lo, "CI high" = hi,
                           "CI width / (3.92 x RSE)" = ratio),
  digits = 3
)
stopifnot(
  all(abs(ci_rows$ratio[1:2] - 2) < 0.25),
  all(abs(ci_rows$ratio[3:8] - 1) < 0.35)
)
```

# Replicating Table 5: target attainment by regimen

Table 5 reports, per regimen, the percentage of simulated children reaching
each exposure target, separately for fast and slow acetylators for isoniazid.
These percentages are per class, so they do not depend on the mixture
proportion. Cmax is the steady-state peak of daily dosing.

```{r table5}
attain <- function(nodes, doses, omega_f, cl_fun, classes, targets) {
  out <- list()
  for (reg in names(doses)) {
    for (cls in classes) {
      nd <- nodes[nodes$MIX_FAST_ELIM == cls, ]
      d <- doses[[reg]](nd$WT)
      for (tg in names(targets)) {
        thr <- targets[[tg]]
        p <- if (tg == "AUC0-24 > 10.5") {
          p_above(1 / cl_fun(nd$WT, cls), d, nd$wq, omega_f, thr)
        } else if (grepl("<", tg, fixed = TRUE)) {
          1 - p_above(nd$cmax1, d, nd$wq, omega_f, thr)
        } else {
          p_above(nd$cmax1, d, nd$wq, omega_f, thr)
        }
        out[[length(out) + 1]] <- data.frame(regimen = reg, class = cls, target = tg, simulated = 100 * p)
      }
    }
  }
  dplyr::bind_rows(out)
}
cl_inh <- function(wt, cls) ifelse(cls == 1, 7.79, 2.59) * (wt / 19.4)^0.75
cl_rif <- function(wt, cls) 8.11 * (wt / 19.4)^0.75

t5_sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  attain(nodes_inh, dose_inh, of_inh, cl_inh, c(1, 0),
         list("Cmax > 6" = 6, "Cmax > 3" = 3, "AUC0-24 > 10.5" = 10.5)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(drug = "Isoniazid", class = ifelse(class == 1, "fast", "slow")),
  attain(nodes_rif, dose_rif, of_rif, cl_rif, 0, list("Cmax > 8" = 8, "Cmax < 4" = 4)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(drug = "Rifampicin", class = "all")
)

# Table 5 of Aruldhas 2019 (blank cells were not simulated by the authors).
t5_pub <- tibble::tribble(
  ~drug, ~class, ~target, ~regimen, ~published,
  "Isoniazid", "fast", "Cmax > 6", "Regimen 1", 41.6,
  "Isoniazid", "fast", "Cmax > 6", "Regimen 2", 47.6,
  "Isoniazid", "fast", "Cmax > 3", "Regimen 1", 88.6,
  "Isoniazid", "fast", "Cmax > 3", "Regimen 2", 90.6,
  "Isoniazid", "fast", "Cmax > 3", "Regimen 3", 84.9,
  "Isoniazid", "fast", "AUC0-24 > 10.5", "Regimen 1", 95.9,
  "Isoniazid", "fast", "AUC0-24 > 10.5", "Regimen 2", 97.1,
  "Isoniazid", "fast", "AUC0-24 > 10.5", "Regimen 3", 94.1,
  "Isoniazid", "slow", "Cmax > 6", "Regimen 1", 60.6,
  "Isoniazid", "slow", "Cmax > 6", "Regimen 2", 73.1,
  "Isoniazid", "slow", "Cmax > 3", "Regimen 1", 95.9,
  "Isoniazid", "slow", "Cmax > 3", "Regimen 2", 98.6,
  "Isoniazid", "slow", "Cmax > 3", "Regimen 3", 94.4,
  "Isoniazid", "slow", "AUC0-24 > 10.5", "Regimen 1", 99.9,
  "Isoniazid", "slow", "AUC0-24 > 10.5", "Regimen 2", 100,
  "Isoniazid", "slow", "AUC0-24 > 10.5", "Regimen 3", 99.9,
  "Rifampicin", "all", "Cmax > 8", "Regimen 1", 15.1,
  "Rifampicin", "all", "Cmax > 8", "Regimen 2", 17.8,

t5 <- dplyr::inner_join(t5_pub, t5_sim, by = c("drug", "class", "target", "regimen")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(diff = simulated - published)

knitr::kable(
  t5 |> dplyr::rename("Drug" = drug, "Acetylator class" = class, "Target (mg/L, mg*h/L)" = target,
                      "Regimen" = regimen, "Published (%)" = published, "Simulated (%)" = simulated,
                      "Difference (points)" = diff),
  digits = 1,
  caption = "Replicates Table 5 of Aruldhas 2019."
)
stopifnot(
  nrow(t5) == nrow(t5_pub),
  abs(median(t5$diff)) < 3,
  max(abs(t5$diff)) < 7
)
```

All 24 published cells are reproduced, with a median difference of
`r sprintf("%.1f", median(t5$diff))` percentage points and a largest absolute
difference of `r sprintf("%.1f", max(abs(t5$diff)))` points. The isoniazid
fast-acetylator cells run 2-5 points high. The paper says the simulated
exposures 'were derived from the posthoc estimates from NONMEM', i.e. from
re-estimated individual parameters of the simulated data. Shrinkage of those
estimates narrows the distribution, which may account for a few points; the
gap is not tuned away. Reading the %CV values as `omega = CV` instead of
the exact `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)` moves the rifampicin cells 2-3 points
further from the published values, which supports the exact conversion used
in the models.

# Replicating Figures 2-4: Cmax and AUC by body weight

Figures 2-4 show box plots of simulated Cmax (and, for isoniazid, AUC0-24)
at each integer weight. The maintainers digitised the medians from the
published figures (precision about +/- 0.3 mg/L, +/- 1 mg h/L). The model
medians below are exact quantiles of the integrated distribution.

```{r fig-medians}
digitised <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(
    figure = "Figure 2A: isoniazid Cmax, Regimen 2",
    WT = c(6, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15, 16, 17, 18, 22, 23, 30),
    digitised = c(6.4, 5.6, 7.2, 5.6, 6.8, 5.6, 6.5, 6.2, 7.0, 5.8, 7.5, 5.7)
  ),
  data.frame(
    figure = "Figure 3: rifampicin Cmax, Regimen 2",
    WT = c(6, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15, 16, 17, 18, 22, 23, 30),
    digitised = c(4.1, 3.7, 4.9, 3.6, 4.55, 3.55, 4.2, 4.0, 4.55, 3.65, 4.75, 3.6)
  ),
  data.frame(
    figure = "Figure 4: rifampicin Cmax, Regimen 4",
    WT = 6:30,
    digitised = c(11.0, 11.9, 12.2, 12.4, 12.3, 12.7, 13.6, 12.2, 11.6, 14.2, 13.5, 13.0, 12.1,
                  11.6, 13.6, 12.7, 12.3, 11.7, 13.4, 13.7, 12.5, 12.4, 13.9, 13.3, 12.8)
  )
)

p_fast_printed <- 0.31

# Median Cmax at one weight. For isoniazid the two acetylator classes are
# mixed in the proportion p_fast through the quadrature weights.
median_cmax <- function(nodes, dose_fun, omega_f, wt, p_fast = NULL) {
  nd <- nodes[nodes$WT == wt, ]
  wq <- nd$wq
  if (!is.null(p_fast)) wq <- wq * ifelse(nd$MIX_FAST_ELIM == 1, p_fast, 1 - p_fast)
  mix_quantile(0.5, nd$cmax1, dose_fun(wt), wq, omega_f)
}
fig_model_median <- function(figure, wt) {
  if (grepl("isoniazid", figure, fixed = TRUE)) {
    median_cmax(nodes_inh, dose_inh[["Regimen 2"]], of_inh, wt, p_fast_printed)
  } else if (grepl("Regimen 2", figure, fixed = TRUE)) {
    median_cmax(nodes_rif, dose_rif[["Regimen 2"]], of_rif, wt)
  } else {
    median_cmax(nodes_rif, dose_rif[["Regimen 4"]], of_rif, wt)
  }
}
fig_cmp <- digitised |>
  dplyr::mutate(model = mapply(fig_model_median, figure, WT)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (model / digitised - 1))

ggplot(fig_cmp, aes(WT)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = digitised, colour = "Digitised from paper")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = model, colour = "Model median")) +
  facet_wrap(~figure, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Body weight (kg)", y = "Median steady-state Cmax (mg/L)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates the medians of Figures 2A, 3 and 4 of Aruldhas 2019.")

fig_cmp |>
  dplyr::group_by(figure) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median_pct_diff = median(pct_diff), max_abs_pct_diff = max(abs(pct_diff))) |>
  dplyr::rename("Figure" = figure, "Median % difference" = median_pct_diff,
                "Largest absolute % difference" = max_abs_pct_diff) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

```{r fig-medians-gate}
rif_cmp <- fig_cmp |> dplyr::filter(grepl("rifampicin", figure))
stopifnot(
  abs(median(rif_cmp$pct_diff)) < 6,
  quantile(abs(rif_cmp$pct_diff), 0.9) < 12
)
```

The rifampicin medians at both regimens follow the published saw-tooth shape
(each weight band's fixed dose spread over a growing body weight) and level.
The isoniazid Cmax median depends on the acetylator mixture; see the next
section.

# Errata: the fast-acetylator fraction

The paper states three times that the mixture model assigned 31% of children
to the fast-acetylator class (Results; Table 3 footnote; Discussion: '30.8%
were found to be fast acetylators and 69.2% to be slow acetylators'). Several
of the paper's own outputs are reproduced only if the proportions are the
other way round, i.e. about 69% of children have the 7.79 L/h clearance.

**Figure 2B (isoniazid AUC0-24, Regimen 2).** CL/F has no between-subject
variability, so `AUC0-24 = F * Dose / CL` is exact and the median at each
weight follows from the mixture proportion alone. The figure's y-axis stops at
80 mg h/L. When the axis limits drop points outside that range before the box
statistics are computed, the boxes describe only the subjects below 80, so the
comparison is shown both with and without that truncation.

```{r mixture-auc}
auc_dig <- data.frame(
  WT = c(6, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15, 16, 17, 18, 22, 23, 30),
  digitised = c(25.5, 23, 29.5, 25, 29.5, 27, 30, 29.5, 32, 29, 35.5, 30.5)
)
auc_median <- function(wt, p_fast, upper) {
  d <- dose_inh[["Regimen 2"]](wt)
  mix_quantile(0.5, 1 / c(cl_inh(wt, 1), cl_inh(wt, 0)), d, c(p_fast, 1 - p_fast), of_inh, upper)
}
auc_cmp <- tidyr::expand_grid(auc_dig, p_fast = c(0.31, 0.69), upper = c(Inf, 80)) |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::mutate(model = auc_median(WT, p_fast, upper)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = model / digitised)
auc_summary <- auc_cmp |>
  dplyr::group_by(p_fast, upper) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median_ratio = median(ratio), min_ratio = min(ratio), max_ratio = max(ratio), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(
  auc_summary |>
    dplyr::mutate(upper = ifelse(is.finite(upper), "points above 80 dropped", "all points"),
                  p_fast = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * p_fast)) |>
    dplyr::rename("Fast-acetylator fraction" = p_fast, "Box statistics over" = upper,
                  "Median model/digitised" = median_ratio, "Min" = min_ratio, "Max" = max_ratio),
  digits = 2
)
printed <- auc_summary |> dplyr::filter(p_fast == 0.31)
swapped_trunc <- auc_summary |> dplyr::filter(p_fast == 0.69, upper == 80)
stopifnot(
  # The printed 31% overpredicts every digitised median, with or without
  # the axis truncation.
  all(printed$min_ratio > 1.2),
  # 69% with the axis truncation reproduces them to within the digitising error.
  abs(swapped_trunc$median_ratio - 1) < 0.08
)

# Median AUC0-24 over the whole 6-30 kg Regimen 2 population, all points.
pop_auc_median <- function(p_fast) {
  wt <- rep(6:30, each = 2)
  cls <- rep(c(1, 0), times = 25)
  mix_quantile(0.5, 1 / cl_inh(wt, cls), dose_inh[["Regimen 2"]](wt),
               ifelse(cls == 1, p_fast, 1 - p_fast), of_inh)
}
pop_auc <- c(printed = pop_auc_median(0.31), swapped = pop_auc_median(0.69))
pop_auc
```

Over the whole 6-30 kg population the median isoniazid AUC0-24 under Regimen 2
is `r sprintf("%.1f", pop_auc[["printed"]])` mg h/L with the printed 31% and
`r sprintf("%.1f", pop_auc[["swapped"]])` mg h/L with 69%.

```{r mixture-auc-gate}
stopifnot(pop_auc[["printed"]] > 1.5 * pop_auc[["swapped"]])
```

**Figure 2A (isoniazid Cmax, Regimen 2).** Cmax depends less on clearance
than AUC does, but the same comparison holds: the printed 31% puts the model
medians above the digitised ones, while 69% brings them close.

```{r mixture-cmax}
cmax_inh_cmp <- fig_cmp |>
  dplyr::filter(grepl("isoniazid", figure)) |>
  dplyr::select(WT, digitised, p31 = model) |>
  dplyr::mutate(p69 = mapply(function(w) median_cmax(nodes_inh, dose_inh[["Regimen 2"]], of_inh, w, 0.69), WT))
cmax_inh_summary <- data.frame(
  p_fast = c("31%", "69%"),
  median_pct_diff = c(median(100 * (cmax_inh_cmp$p31 / cmax_inh_cmp$digitised - 1)),
                      median(100 * (cmax_inh_cmp$p69 / cmax_inh_cmp$digitised - 1)))
)
knitr::kable(
  cmax_inh_summary |>
    dplyr::rename("Fast-acetylator fraction" = p_fast, "Median % difference from digitised" = median_pct_diff),
  digits = 1
)
stopifnot(
  abs(cmax_inh_summary$median_pct_diff[2]) < abs(cmax_inh_summary$median_pct_diff[1])
)
```

**Table 3 secondary parameters.** The posthoc median AUC0-24 of the studied
children was 34.04 mg h/L (IQR 23.29-44.23). At a typical Regimen 2 dose for
a 19.4-kg child (225 mg), a slow acetylator has `AUC0-24 = 225 / 2.59 =
87` mg h/L and a fast acetylator `225 / 7.79 = 29` mg h/L; a median of 34
is possible only if most children are in the fast class. The rifampicin value
from the same children and the same mg dose, `225 / 8.11 = 28` against a
published median of 25.19, shows the doses are not the explanation.

**Table 5 pooled percentages.** For Regimen 3 the Results report that about
88% of all children reach Cmax > 3 mg/L and 96% reach AUC0-24 > 10.5. Solving
`p x fast + (1 - p) x slow` for the class-specific cells of Table 5 gives
`p = (94.4 - 88) / (94.4 - 84.9) = 0.67` and `p = (99.9 - 96) / (99.9 - 94.1)
= 0.67` for the fast fraction.

**Figure 1A (isoniazid VPC).** The observed median falls from about 4.3 mg/L
at 2.5 h to about 1.3 mg/L at 6 h, an apparent elimination rate near
0.34 /h; the slow-acetylator rate is `2.59 / 29.7 = 0.087` /h and the fast
one `7.79 / 29.7 = 0.26` /h. Most pre-dose concentrations sit near the
0.01 mg/L LLOQ, whereas a slow acetylator on daily dosing would have a trough
near 1 mg/L.

The model file encodes the published clearances unchanged, and they are what
Table 5 validates per class. The class probability is not a model parameter:
it is used only when drawing `MIX_FAST_ELIM` for a virtual cohort. The
`MIX_FAST_ELIM` notes in the model file carry the printed 31%. Users who want
to reproduce the paper's own population-level outputs should note that those
outputs correspond to about 69% of children in the fast (7.79 L/h) class.

# Virtual cohort and PKNCA

A stochastic cohort reproduces the steady-state profile under Regimen 2 daily
dosing, the regimen given to the studied children. Weights cover the paper's
simulated range of 6-30 kg (eight children per integer kg, 200 per drug).
Isoniazid acetylator classes are assigned with the printed 31% fast fraction.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20190301)
n_per <- 200
cohort <- data.frame(id = seq_len(n_per), WT = rep(6:30, length.out = n_per))
set.seed(20190301)
cohort$MIX_FAST_ELIM <- as.integer(seq_len(n_per) %in% sample.int(n_per, round(p_fast_printed * n_per)))

make_events <- function(cohort, dose_fun) {
  dose_times <- seq(0, 24 * 14, by = 24)
  obs_times <- sort(unique(c(24 * 14 + seq(0, 24, by = 0.25), 24 * 14 + c(0.5, 1.5, 2.5))))
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    expand.grid(id = cohort$id, time = dose_times) |>
      dplyr::mutate(evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
    expand.grid(id = cohort$id, time = obs_times) |>
      dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    dplyr::left_join(cohort, by = "id") |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = ifelse(evid == 1L, dose_fun(WT), 0)) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}
ev_inh <- make_events(cohort, dose_inh[["Regimen 2"]])
ev_rif <- make_events(cohort, dose_rif[["Regimen 2"]])

sim_c_inh <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_inh, ev_inh, returnType = "data.frame", keep = c("WT", "MIX_FAST_ELIM"))
sim_c_rif <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_rif, ev_rif, returnType = "data.frame", keep = "WT")
sim_c <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_c_inh |> dplyr::mutate(treatment = "Isoniazid"),
  sim_c_rif |> dplyr::mutate(treatment = "Rifampicin")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = time - 24 * 14)
```

```{r cohort-plot}
sim_c |>
  dplyr::filter(tad <= 6) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, tad) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), p50 = quantile(Cc, 0.5), p95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose at steady state (h)", y = "Plasma concentration (mg/L)",
       caption = "Median and 90% interval over 0-6 h, the sampling window of Figure 1.")
```

```{r pknca}
conc_df <- sim_c |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  ev_inh |> dplyr::filter(evid == 1L) |> dplyr::mutate(treatment = "Isoniazid"),
  ev_rif |> dplyr::filter(evid == 1L) |> dplyr::mutate(treatment = "Rifampicin")
) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 24 * 14, end = 24 * 15, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- suppressMessages(PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals)))

nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, id, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

# Steady-state AUC over one dosing interval equals F * Dose / CL exactly;
# the trapezoidal NCA on a 0.25-h grid must agree to within numerical error.
auc_chk <- nca_wide |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    dplyr::bind_rows(
      sim_c_inh |> dplyr::mutate(treatment = "Isoniazid"),
      sim_c_rif |> dplyr::mutate(treatment = "Rifampicin")
    ) |>
      dplyr::filter(time == 24 * 14) |>
      dplyr::select(treatment, id, WT, cl),
    by = c("treatment", "id")
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dose_df |> dplyr::distinct(treatment, id, amt), by = c("treatment", "id"))
```

The per-subject bioavailability is not an output column, so the closed form
is checked on the subjects' ratio `AUC0-24 x CL / Dose`, which must equal
their individual F: its spread must match the F omega.

```{r pknca-check}
auc_chk <- auc_chk |> dplyr::mutate(f_implied = auclast * cl / amt)
f_sd <- auc_chk |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(sd_log_f = sd(log(f_implied)), median_f = median(f_implied), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(
  f_sd |> dplyr::rename("Drug" = treatment, "SD of log implied F" = sd_log_f, "Median implied F" = median_f),
  digits = 3
)
stopifnot(
  # Monte Carlo SE of an SD at n = 200 is about 5%; 15% is three SEs.
  abs(f_sd$sd_log_f[f_sd$treatment == "Isoniazid"] / of_inh - 1) < 0.15,
  abs(f_sd$sd_log_f[f_sd$treatment == "Rifampicin"] / of_rif - 1) < 0.15
)
```

# Comparison against the published secondary parameters

Tables 3 and 4 report the median of the posthoc Cmax, Tmax and AUC0-24 of the
studied children. The simulated cohort is the paper's 6-30 kg simulation
population rather than the 39 studied children, so close agreement is not
expected; the comparison is a check of level.

```{r nca-compare}
reference <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("Isoniazid", "Rifampicin"),
  cmax = c(5.90, 4.73),
  tmax = c(1.10, 1.59),
  auclast = c(34.04, 25.19)
)
sim_long <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, id, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  sim_long, reference,
  by = "treatment",
  params = c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast"),
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L", tmax = "h", auclast = "mg*h/L")
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Steady-state AUC0-24 is reported as `auclast` over the 24-h interval.")
```

Rifampicin Cmax, Tmax and AUC0-24 agree with Table 4. Isoniazid Tmax agrees;
the simulated isoniazid AUC0-24 is well above the published median, which is
the acetylator-fraction inconsistency described in the Errata section above
(the population medians under both readings are computed in that section).

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Transit convention.** `ktr = (n + 1) / MTT` with the absorption rate equal
  to the transit rate; confirmed against the published Tmax.
* **BSV conversion.** `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`; the paper does not state the
  formula. The Table 5 replication favours it over `omega = CV`.
* **Residual error.** The 'RUV' rows are read as variances (CI-width argument
  above). Residual error is `lnorm(expSd)`, the exact counterpart of an
  additive error on log-transformed concentrations.
* **Reference weight.** 19.4 kg, the typical child of the Tables 3 and 4
  footnotes (Table 2 gives a median of 19.5 kg for all 41 enrolled children).
* **Table 5 simulation design.** Daily dosing to steady state at every integer
  weight from 6 to 30 kg, with the Table 1 weight-band doses. The paper used
  Cmax > 6 mg/L as the target for thrice-weekly dosing but does not say
  whether those cells were simulated with a thrice-weekly schedule; simulating
  them thrice weekly lowers the slow-acetylator cells by about 11 points
  (fast-acetylator cells are unchanged) and fits the published values less
  well, so daily dosing is used throughout.
* **Regimen 4, 6-11 kg.** 35 mg/kg as the commercially available suspension
  (Table 1 footnote), simulated with the same bioavailability as the capsules.
* **Fast-acetylator fraction.** The printed 31% is carried in the model
  metadata; the paper's own exposure outputs instead correspond to about 69%
  (Errata section above). No parameter was changed.
* **Auto-induction.** Not modelled. Samples were taken after about 60 days of
  rifampicin, so the rifampicin model describes the induced steady state only
  and should not be used for the first weeks of therapy.
* **Covariates screened but not retained.** Age, sex, body mass index,
  height, albumin and fat-free mass (as an alternative size descriptor) are
  listed in `covariatesDataExcluded`.
